turns.prompt: My basil plants keep dying on the windowsill. Can you explain what basil actually needs?
turns.response:
Basil wants **sun, warmth, and moist soil that drains freely**. A windowsill can provide the sun while quietly failing on the warmth. ([rhs.org.uk](https://www.rhs.org.uk/herbs/basil/grow-your-own?utm_source=openai))

Here’s what matters:

- **Strong light.** Aim for roughly six hours of direct sunlight, not just a room that looks bright. In darker months, a grow light may be needed even beside a window. ([eauclaire.extension.wisc.edu](https://eauclaire.extension.wisc.edu/files/2011/03/MiniHerbWorkshop2015.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- **Warmth without cold drafts.** Keep it away from a cold windowpane and chilly overnight conditions. Basil is less forgiving of a cool sill than many other herbs. ([chicagobotanic.org](https://www.chicagobotanic.org/plantinfo/tips/growing_herbs_your_windowsill?utm_source=openai))
- **Water according to the soil, not a schedule.** Let the surface begin to dry before watering again; don’t keep the root ball constantly saturated. Use a pot with drainage holes, let excess water escape, and don’t leave it standing in water. Wet roots need air, too. ([ask.extension.org](https://ask.extension.org/kb/faq.php?id=904518&utm_source=openai))
- **Room to grow.** If yours are supermarket pots, they often contain lots of overcrowded seedlings intended for short-term harvesting. Dividing and repotting them can help; their rapid decline isn’t necessarily your fault. ([rhs.org.uk](https://www.rhs.org.uk/herbs/basil/grow-your-own))
- **Regular trimming.** Snip stems just above a pair of leaves to encourage branching, and remove flower buds to keep it producing leaves. Feed indoor plants lightly—half-strength liquid fertilizer every four to six weeks is the extension service’s guidance. ([extension.umn.edu](https://extension.umn.edu/garden-and-home/yard-and-garden/yard-and-garden-problems/growing-basil))

What happens first with yours: what do the leaves and stems look like when they start going downhill?

turns.prompt: How often should I water it, and how do I tell if I'm overdoing it?
turns.response:
**Check it daily, but don’t water it automatically.** Basil wants evenly moist soil—not a permanently soggy pot. How quickly it dries depends on the pot, light and warmth, so a fixed weekly schedule isn’t reliable. ([rhs.org.uk](https://www.rhs.org.uk/herbs/basil/grow-your-own?type=h&utm_source=openai))

- **Feel the soil before watering.** If the surface is beginning to dry, water; if it’s still moist, wait. Don’t let the whole root ball dry out. ([extension.umd.edu](https://extension.umd.edu/resource/watering-indoor-plants?utm_source=openai))
- **Water thoroughly, then let it drain.** Use a pot with drainage holes and empty the saucer rather than leaving the roots standing in water. ([extension.umd.edu](https://extension.umd.edu/resource/watering-indoor-plants?utm_source=openai))

**Signs you may be overdoing it:**
- Yellowing or dropping leaves while the soil stays wet.
- Wilting despite damp soil—drooping doesn’t always mean thirst.
- Soft, mushy stems, which can indicate rot. ([extension.umd.edu](https://www.extension.umd.edu/resource/overwatered-indoor-plants?utm_source=openai))

The useful distinction is **wilting + dry soil versus wilting + wet soil**. Check before adding another drink; damaged, waterlogged roots can’t supply the leaves properly either. ([yardandgarden.extension.iastate.edu](https://yardandgarden.extension.iastate.edu/faq/why-my-houseplant-wilting?utm_source=openai))

turns.prompt: Is it worth trying to grow it from seed, or are supermarket pots fine to keep going?
turns.response:
**Supermarket pots can keep going—you don’t have to start from seed.** The catch is that they’re usually a crowd of seedlings packed together for short-term harvesting, rather than a well-spaced plant meant to grow on. Dividing and repotting them promptly gives them a better chance. ([rhs.org.uk](https://www.rhs.org.uk/herbs/basil/grow-your-own))

- **For the quickest route:** buy a healthy supermarket pot, gently separate it into smaller clumps and repot in fresh potting mix, using pots with drainage holes. Don’t wait until it’s collapsing. ([tollbit.gardenersworld.com](https://tollbit.gardenersworld.com/how-to/grow-plants/how-to-make-five-plants-from-one-supermarket-basil?utm_source=openai))
- **For growing from scratch:** seed is worth trying, particularly for a wider choice of varieties. Sow thinly in seed compost and keep warm—around **20°C / 68°F** for germination. You can sow small batches a few weeks apart rather than relying on one plant indefinitely. ([rhs.org.uk](https://www.rhs.org.uk/herbs/basil/grow-your-own))

**I’d try dividing a supermarket pot first.** But seed isn’t a workaround for an unsuitable windowsill: either route still needs warmth and plenty of light. We haven’t yet established what’s killing yours. ([rhs.org.uk](https://www.rhs.org.uk/herbs/basil/grow-your-own))
